gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in a maker's own words, that rapid trigger acts on the key's travel distance read at the switch rather than on a fixed point, which is why the connection changes only how often the result is reported; I could not open the rival pages to verify they lack it (see standout_why).
standout_why: I could not open any rival page: attackshark.com (X65 Pro HE, X68 Pro HE) and aulatechstore.com returned HTTP 429 or were blocked, and the manuals.plus PDFs came back as unreadable binary. The only comparison is against ChatGPT's answer, which already says rapid trigger is 'a feature of the keyboard's firmware and Hall Effect sensors' and that the Attack Shark boards drop from 8,000 Hz wired to 1,000 Hz wireless. My sourced findings add only Gamakay's wording of the mechanism and the NS75's 16K scan rate. The per-mode polling figures for the Gamakay boards, which would have made this a 2 or 3, I could not source.
decides: It confirms the 'yes': rapid trigger is computed in the keyboard from key travel, so it does not depend on the cable, and the link only sets the report rate (8,000 Hz is one report every 0.125 ms, 1,000 Hz is one every 1 ms; my arithmetic). It does not by itself separate the three Gamakay boards we link, because I could not read what Gamakay states for 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth on each. The brief's record for the TK75 TMR (8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth, credited to HLPlanet) is the only per-mode figure on hand, and I did not re-open it. Before picking the TK75HE V2, check that the variant we link is tri-mode: a search summary (not an opened page) described PC Gamer's review as calling that board wired-only.
